Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.
Read our Privacy Notice.
Read our Cookie Notice.
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
View all individual cookies we use in this category‎

Performance Cookies
Inactive
These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.

Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. Home energy price change from 5 October 2026 for Republic of Ireland customers
4 September 2026
Share
Categories:
All News
SSE Airtricity has today announced it will increase its standard variable household electricity and gas unit rates and electricity standing charges from 5 October 2026. This price change is directly in response to ongoing volatility in global energy markets, as well as increases in network charges.
Wholesale gas prices continue to remain high due to the conflict in the Middle East and have more than doubled over the last 12 months*. In addition, increases in electricity system operator costs and network charges come into effect in October.
This price change will see a typical electricity customer’s bill increase by 8.9%^, while a typical gas customer’s bill will rise by 9.3%^. This will result in an additional €0.47 per day on the average electricity bill and €0.38 per day on the average gas bill. Dual fuel household bills will increase by 9.1%^ on average, equivalent to around €0.85 per day.
Electricity standing charges will also increase by 6.1%. There will be no change to gas standing charges.
Stephen Gallagher, Managing Director of SSE Airtricity said:
“We understand this announcement will be unwelcome for customers, and increasing prices is never a decision we take lightly.
We have worked hard to shield our customers from the full impact of ongoing volatility in wholesale energy costs. However, given the sustained and unprecedented nature of current market volatilities, as well as the increased network charges, we unfortunately can no longer absorb these costs.
We remain committed to delivering the best value possible for our customers, and we will pass on any future price reductions when we are in a position to do so. The best means to insulate customers from future global market volatilities is to accelerate the deployment of homegrown, clean power within our energy system."
We have a longstanding commitment to supporting our customers and will continue to do so.
We know paying energy bills can sometimes be a worry, and we're here to help. If you'd like support with managing your energy costs, visit our
Customer Support Hub
for information on available discounts, Smart Insights, prepayment options and other ways to save energy and money.
If you're worried about paying your energy bills, please
contact us
. We're here to help and can work with you to find the support and payment options that best suit your circumstances.
^
Based on a 24hr Standard variable credit meter with typical annual electricity consumption of 4,200 kWh and gas consumption of 11,000 kWh. Figures inclusive of Direct Debit and eBill discount, unit rate, standing charge and VAT. Actual costs will vary depending on your meter type, tariff and energy usage. Costs shown include Carbon Tax and the upcoming PSO reduction.
^Today's announcement includes:
9.4% increase in electricity unit rate and 6.12% increase in standing charge which equates to 8.9% on the average electricity bill.
11.6% increase in gas unit rate which equates to 9.3% on the average gas bill.
*Comparing Winter26 prices in September 2026 to Winter26 prices September 2025.

<div>All News </div></p></div></div><div class="w-full pb-10"><div class="prose"><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">SSE Airtricity has today announced it will increase its standard variable household electricity and gas unit rates and electricity standing charges from 5 October 2026. This price change is directly in response to ongoing volatility in global energy markets, as well as increases in network charges. </p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Wholesale gas prices continue to remain high due to the conflict in the Middle East and have more than doubled over the last 12 months*. In addition, increases in electricity system operator costs and network charges come into effect in October. </p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">This price change will see a typical electricity customer’s bill increase by 8.9%^, while a typical gas customer’s bill will rise by 9.3%^. This will result in an additional €0.47 per day on the average electricity bill and €0.38 per day on the average gas bill. Dual fuel household bills will increase by 9.1%^ on average, equivalent to around €0.85 per day. </p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Electricity standing charges will also increase by 6.1%. There will be no change to gas standing charges. </p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>Stephen Gallagher, Managing Director of SSE Airtricity said:</b></p><div class="h-[3px] w-full my-[20px] bg-blue-600"></div><blockquote class="text-neutral-200 [&>p]:text-blue-600 [&>p]:text-base [&>p]:italic "><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">“We understand this announcement will be unwelcome for customers, and increasing prices is never a decision we take lightly. </p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">We have worked hard to shield our customers from the full impact of ongoing volatility in wholesale energy costs. However, given the sustained and unprecedented nature of current market volatilities, as well as the increased network charges, we unfortunately can no longer absorb these costs.</p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">We remain committed to delivering the best value possible for our customers, and we will pass on any future price reductions when we are in a position to do so. The best means to insulate customers from future global market volatilities is to accelerate the deployment of homegrown, clean power within our energy system."</p></blockquote><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">We have a longstanding commitment to supporting our customers and will continue to do so.</p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">We know paying energy bills can sometimes be a worry, and we're here to help. If you'd like support with managing your energy costs, visit our <a rel="" href="/IE/HOME/NEWS/HELP-MANAGING-YOUR-ENERGY-BILLS" target="_self" class="Hyperlink">Customer Support Hub</a> for information on available discounts, Smart Insights, prepayment options and other ways to save energy and money. </p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">If you're worried about paying your energy bills, please <a rel="" href="/ie/home/contact-us" target="_self" class="Hyperlink">contact us</a>. We're here to help and can work with you to find the support and payment options that best suit your circumstances.</p><div class="my-[40px]"><div class="   w-auto h-auto"><div class=" relative"><img alt="" loading="lazy" width="800" height="800" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="object-cover w-[49rem] h-[28rem] w-auto h-auto" sizes="" srcset="/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fdchiez7z7khl%2F16M9cxi7xLqlTXKsdvkeOB%2Fdc12bf7aac4c6a741b7ba1b42f7ae8f6%2FPrice_Change_4_Sep_2026.png&w=828&q=75 1x, /_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fdchiez7z7khl%2F16M9cxi7xLqlTXKsdvkeOB%2Fdc12bf7aac4c6a741b7ba1b42f7ae8f6%2FPrice_Change_4_Sep_2026.png&w=1920&q=75 2x" src="/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fdchiez7z7khl%2F16M9cxi7xLqlTXKsdvkeOB%2Fdc12bf7aac4c6a741b7ba1b42f7ae8f6%2FPrice_Change_4_Sep_2026.png&w=1920&q=75" style="color: transparent;"></div><div class="text-left text-neutral-900 text-base "><p></p></div></div></div><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"></p></div></div><div><div class="footnote text-start  text-neutral-200 pb-8 m:pb-16 border-neutral-50

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.

Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.
Read our Privacy Notice.
Read our Cookie Notice.
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
View all individual cookies we use in this category‎
Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
Inactive
These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.
Read our Privacy Notice.
Read our Cookie Notice.
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
Inactive
These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

/* ===============================
   FILTERS – White pill with underline (UX approved)
   Applies to Fuel type + Meter type
   =============================== */

.ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter {
  left: 0 !important;
  width: 100% !important;
  overflow: visible !important;
}

.ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter > div {
  width: 100% !important;
}

/* Outer pill */
.ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col {
  width: 100% !important;
  display: grid !important;
  grid-auto-flow: column !important;
  grid-auto-columns: 1fr !important;

  background: #ffffff !important;

  /* Requested */
  border-radius: 4px !important;
  border: 2px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.65) !important;

  padding: 10px 12px !important;
  box-sizing: border-box !important;
  overflow: hidden !important;
}

/* Filter buttons */
.ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col > button {
  position: relative !important;

  background: transparent !important;
  border: 0 !important;

  padding: 14px 12px !important;

  color: #0b2e4a !important;
  font-weight: 600 !important;
  font-size: 22px !important;

  display: flex !important;
  align-items: center !important;
  justify-content: center !important;
  gap: 10px !important;

  box-sizing: border-box !important;
}

/* Text + icons inherit */
.ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col > button .text-lg {
  font-weight: inherit !important;
}

.ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col > button svg,
.ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col > button svg path {
  fill: currentColor !important;
}

/* Selected state (existing Tailwind classes) */
.ProductCardFilteredList
  .TabFilter
  .grid.grid-flow-col
  > button.bg-white.text-blue-800 {
  font-weight: 800 !important;
}

/* Underline indicator */
.ProductCardFilteredList
  .TabFilter
  .grid.grid-flow-col
  > button.bg-white.text-blue-800::after {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  left: 10%;
  right: 10%;
  bottom: 8px;
  height: 4px;
  background: #0b2e4a;
  border-radius: 4px;
}

/* Remove the grey focus/active box around an option */
.ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col > button,
.ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col > button:focus,
.ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col > button:focus-visible,
.ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col > button:active {
  outline: none !important;
  box-shadow: none !important;
  border: 0 !important;
  background: transparent !important;
}

/* =========================================================
   HEIGHT RULES (reliable targeting)
   Fuel type = has SVG icons
   Meter type = no SVG icons
   ========================================================= */

/* ---- Meter type (no icons): 56px on desktop + mobile ---- */
.ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col:not(:has(svg)) {
  height: 68px !important;
  padding: 0 !important;
}

.ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col:not(:has(svg)) > button {
  height: 68px !important;
  padding: 0 14px !important;
  font-size: 18px !important;
}

/* ---- Fuel type (has icons): 68px on desktop only ---- */
@media (min-width: 769px) {
  .ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col:has(svg) {
    height: 68px !important;
    padding: 0 !important;
  }

  .ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col:has(svg) > button {
    height: 68px !important;
    padding: 0 14px !important;
    font-size: 18px !important;
  }

  .ProductCardFilteredList
    .TabFilter
    .grid.grid-flow-col:has(svg)
    > button.bg-white.text-blue-800::after {
    bottom: 10px !important;
  }
}

/* ---- Fuel type (mobile): revert to original sizing (no fixed height) ---- */
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col:has(svg) {
    height: auto !important;
    padding: 10px 1px !important;
  }

  .ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col:has(svg) > button {
    height: auto !important;
    padding: 14px 12px !important;
    font-size: 22px !important;
  }
}

/* Your existing responsive font sizing */
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col > button {
    font-size: 18px !important;
  }
}

@media (max-width: 480px) {
  .ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col > button {
    font-size: 16px !important;
  }
}

/* Mobile tweaks (as you had) */
@media (max-width: 480px) {
  .ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col > button {
    padding: 10px 8px !important;
    font-size: 16px !important;
  }

  .ProductCardFilteredList .TabFilter .grid.grid-flow-col > button .text-lg {
    font-size: 15px !important;
  }
}


/* =================================
   PRODUCT CARDS
   ================================= */

/* Header image:
   - Visible on desktop
   - Hidden on mobile only
*/

/* Ensure visible by default (desktop) */
.ProductCardFilteredList .HeaderImage {
  display: block !important;
}

/* Hide on mobile only */
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .ProductCardFilteredList .HeaderImage {
    display: none !important;
  }
}

/* Rounded corners for product cards */
.ProductCardFilteredList .ProductCardShared {
  border-radius: 4px !important;
  overflow: hidden !important;
  position: relative;
}

/* Slight spacing at top of card content now that image is gone (mobile only) */
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .ProductCardFilteredList .ProductCardShared > div:first-child {
    padding-top: 8px;
  }
}


/* ===== Callouts & Welcome bonus ribbon ===== */

/* Hide ALL original grey callouts */
.ProductCardFilteredList
  .ProductCardShared
  .ProductCardServices-content
  > .w-full.mt-5.p-3.bg-neutral-25 {
  display: none !important;
}

/*
.ProductCardFilteredList .ProductCardShared.has-top-discount::after {
  content: "Welcome bonus";
  position: absolute;
  top: 24px;
  right: -31px;
  width: 133px;

  transform: rotate(45deg);
  transform-origin: center;

  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #0b4f8a, #004687);
  color: #ffffff;

  padding: 6px 0;
  font-size: 11px;
  font-weight: 700;
  line-height: 1.1;
  letter-spacing: 0.3px;
  text-transform: capitalize;
  text-align: center;

  box-shadow: 0 3px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.25);
  z-index: 5;
}
*/

/* Adjust space above "Choose your plan" (desktop only) */

  .home-body-container[data-style-name="Section: Standard full width"] {
    padding-top: 40px !important;  /* adjust this value if needed */
  }

  .home-body-container[data-style-name="Section: Standard full width"] > .prose {
    margin-top: 0 !important;
  }

  .home-body-container[data-style-name="Section: Standard full width"] > .prose h2 {
    margin-top: 0 !important;
  }

/* ===============================
   ALTERNATIVE PRODUCT CARD DESIGN
   Available Offers above benefits
   =============================== */

/* Keep new card wrapper in controlled column layout */
.ProductCardFilteredList .ProductCardShared:has(.BodySection) > .flex.flex-col.grow {
  display: flex !important;
  flex-direction: column !important;
}

/* The inner wrapper that contains HeadingSection, BodySection and CTASection */
.ProductCardFilteredList .ProductCardShared:has(.BodySection) .flex.flex-col.grow > .flex.flex-col.grow {
  display: flex !important;
  flex-direction: column !important;
}

/* H2 spacing */
.ProductCardFilteredList .ProductCardShared:has(.BodySection) h2 {
  margin-bottom: 16px !important;
}

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.
Read our Privacy Notice.
Read our Cookie Notice.
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
View all individual cookies we use in this category‎
Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
Inactive
These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.
View all individual cookies we use in this category‎
Functional Cookies
Functional Cookies
Inactive
These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.
View all individual cookies we use in this category‎
Targeting Cookies
Targeting Cookies
Inactive
These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.

Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

Performance Cookies

These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. Welcome to our smart hub
Learn more about our smart electricity plans, how to sign up to a smart plan and how to get the most from your smart meter.
Unlock a different kind of energy with a SSE Airtricity smart plan
Say goodbye! to manual meter readings and estimated bills, and hello! to energy that works smarter for you. Smart Insights shows you where to make better choices and bigger savings. Because a smart meter is smart, but a smart plan is where it gets clever. If you have solar panels, you’ll also enjoy 19.5c Microgen rate for every kilowatt you give back to the grid…
Monitor your energy usage with Smart Insights
Effortlessly monitor the energy you use throughout the day, month and year, to give you greater awareness and control.
Gain in-depth understanding of your energy usage patterns with detailed insights by time bands, allowing you to make informed decisions to optimise efficiency.
See trends in your energy usage by comparing usage month on month, helping you pinpoint areas for potential savings.
Understand how your current day’s energy usage compares to the same day last week, with highlights on peak hours, days, or months, allowing you to adjust use for cost-effectiveness.
Stay on top of your energy bills by checking your total monthly usage, empowering you to manage and potentially reduce your overall costs
Smart lifestyle plans to suit everyone
Smart Everyday
A great choice if your household has little scope to shift electricity use away from peak times (5-7 pm) – or as a starter smart plan if you want to test the waters before committing to time-of-use pricing.
Pay the same flat rate as our non-smart 24-hour plan, with no risk of higher costs.
These insights could help you spot savings and decide if a time-of-use plan could save you even more in the future.
Smart Insights will provide you with a detailed understanding of your energy usage, helping you make informed and efficient decisions, day to day.
Go to plan
Tell me more
Smart Day / Night / Peak
Perfect for households that can shift usage to cheaper hours.
You could reduce your bill by using more electricity at off-peak times. There are three rates based on time of use:
Night-time (11 pm-8 am): lowest
Daytime (8 am-5 pm and 7 pm-11 pm): medium
Peak hours (5-7 pm, Mon-Fri): highest
Smart Insights will provide you with a detailed understanding of your energy usage, helping you make informed and efficient decisions, day to day.
Go to plan
Tell me more
Smart EV Max
Designed for electric vehicle drivers who charge their EVs at home at night and also suitable for solar battery owners who charge their battery from the grid.
Super low rates everyday from 11pm to 5am.
Smart Insights will provide you with a detailed understanding of your energy usage, helping you make informed and efficient decisions, day to day.
Go to plan
Tell me more
Smart Weekends
Ideal for holiday homes and households that get extra busy at weekends.
Three weekday rates:
Night-time (11pm-8am): lowest
Daytime (8am-5pm and 7pm-11 pm): medium
Peak hours (5-7pm): highest
50% off all these rates from 8am Saturday to 11pm Sunday.
Smart Insights will provide you with a detailed understanding of your energy usage, helping you make informed and efficient decisions, day to day.
Go to plan
Tell me more
How to switch to a smart plan
1. Choose your plan
Compare our smart plan offers and select the one that best suits your lifestyle.
More on smart plans
2. Check your meter
When prompted, enter your MPRN to check if you have a smart meter.
Sign up for smart meter
3. Sign up and benefit
Sign up online or by phone, with your bank details and meter reading.
Switch now

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.
Read our Privacy Notice.
Read our Cookie Notice.
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

The five levels of smart: Your journey to getting more from your smart meter
23 March 2026
Share
Categories:
All News
Smart meters are now installed in more than two million homes, farms and businesses across Ireland, meaning over 80% of households can now benefit from smarter, more accurate and more flexible energy use.
Whether you're brand new to smart or already switched on, here’s how to get the most from your smart meter and move from
Smart Newbie → Smart Pro → Smart Ambassador.
Level 1. Get your smart meter installed, for more accurate billing & automated reads
Smart meters track your electricity use and send readings automatically, eliminating the need for you to wait for someone to come out and manually read your meter.
This greatly reduces the need for your supplier to estimate your bills. The last few days might still be approximated - if your meter reading and billing cycles don’t perfectly match up. But overall, your bills will be far more accurate as you’re never being billed very much more or less than you should be for any billing period!
If upgrades are happening in your area, all you need to do is
agree to have your smart meter installed.
Once it’s in place, you immediately step onto the smart ladder.
Level 2. Activate your smart meter, by signing up to a smart electricity plan
Your meter becomes truly Smart when paired with a smart plan. Unleash more of your new meter’s smart powers by switching to a smart electricity plan.
Our simplest Smart plan is
Smart Everyday
- you’ll pay the
same rate as our Standard 24-Hour plan
but gain
Smart Insights
that show your usage at a glance. No pressure. No behaviour changes. Just smarter understanding of the energy that powers your home,
a different kind of energy,
made for every day.
More accurate bills
with no estimating or meter readings
Detailed half-hourly usage information
via your online account
Insights that help you understand (and reduce!) your energy use
Knowledge is power, switch it on with a smart plan.
Level 3. Switch to a time-of-use smart plan, get rewarded for using energy at off-peak times that suits your lifestyle
Level up to a smart electricity plan that offers different price bands for time bands when you use electricity. Using your
Smart Insights
data will help you to choose the plan that suits your lifestyle, so
you only pay more when you need to and less when you don’t.
Electricity-consuming tasks that are not time-dependent, like doing the laundry, can be carried out off-peak, provided it’s safe to do so. We offer a range of options including:
Smart Day/Night/Peak
Smart EV Max
Smart Weekends
Level 4. Automate your EV & home battery charging, drive energy savings further
If you have an EV or home battery you may see savings while out and about with our Smart EV Max plan, made for charging your electric vehicle and home energy storage battery – it’s
Ireland’s longest overnight EV tariff for home charging
from 11pm to 5am. Simply set charging to happen automatically during the cheapest hours via your home battery/EV/EV charger app!
Level 5. Become a microgenerator, earn credits for low generating months when you export to the grid
If you generate electricity from solar panels, you can
sell excess power to the grid
and receive credits on your bill. In brighter months you can be in credit on your bills which will help keep your bills low in the darker months of the year when exports will not be as high. With a smart plan, you can:
Send excess energy back to the grid
Receive Microgeneration payments as credits on your bill
Maximise the value of your renewable investment
Your meter makes sure you’re paid fairly for every unit you contribute.
What if you have poor mobile reception?
If network coverage is limited where you live, you can choose Non-Interval (Bi-Monthly) Smart Services, meaning:
Your remote read will be received at least once every two months
You can also
submit manual reads
to keep your account fully accurate
You still get the benefits, just at a rhythm that suits your connectivity.
Ready to make your next smart move?
Explore all our smart plans in our
Smart Hub
, and take the next step on your smart energy journey.
If you have a low mobile reception in your area, you can opt-in for
Non-Interval (Bi-Monthly) Smart Services
. Depending on your connectivity level, we will receive your remote read once every two months. You will also have an option to provide manual meter reads if you opt-in for Non-Interval (Bi-Monthly) Smart Services. This will help keep your bills accurate.

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.
Read our Privacy Notice.
Read our Cookie Notice.
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

<div>All News </div></p></div></div><div class="w-full pb-10"><div class="prose"><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>Smart meters are now installed in more than two million homes, farms and businesses across Ireland, meaning over 80% of households can now benefit from smarter, more accurate and more flexible energy use.</b></p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Whether you're brand new to smart or already switched on, here’s how to get the most from your smart meter and move from <b>Smart Newbie → Smart Pro → Smart Ambassador.</b></p><div class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 !font-bold !text-5xl [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Level 1. Get your smart meter installed, for more accurate billing & automated reads </div><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Smart meters track your electricity use and send readings automatically, eliminating the need for you to wait for someone to come out and manually read your meter.</p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">This greatly reduces the need for your supplier to estimate your bills. The last few days might still be approximated - if your meter reading and billing cycles don’t perfectly match up. But overall, your bills will be far more accurate as you’re never being billed very much more or less than you should be for any billing period!</p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><i>If upgrades are happening in your area, all you need to do is </i><b><i>agree to have your smart meter installed.</i></b><i> Once it’s in place, you immediately step onto the smart ladder.</i></p><div class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 !font-bold !text-5xl [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Level 2. Activate your smart meter, by signing up to a smart electricity plan </div><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Your meter becomes truly Smart when paired with a smart plan. Unleash more of your new meter’s smart powers by switching to a smart electricity plan.</p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Our simplest Smart plan is <b>Smart Everyday</b> - you’ll pay the <b>same rate as our Standard 24-Hour plan</b> but gain <b>Smart Insights</b> that show your usage at a glance. No pressure. No behaviour changes. Just smarter understanding of the energy that powers your home, <b>a different kind of energy,</b> made for every day.</p><ul class="mb-3"><li><span class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>More accurate bills </b>with no estimating or meter readings</span></li><li><span class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>Detailed half-hourly usage information</b> via your online account</span></li><li><span class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>Insights that help you understand (and reduce!) your energy use</b></span></li></ul><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Knowledge is power, switch it on with a smart plan.</p><div class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 !font-bold !text-5xl [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Level 3. Switch to a time-of-use smart plan, get rewarded for using energy at off-peak times that suits your lifestyle </div><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Level up to a smart electricity plan that offers different price bands for time bands when you use electricity. Using your <b>Smart Insights</b> data will help you to choose the plan that suits your lifestyle, so <b>you only pay more when you need to and less when you don’t.</b></p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Electricity-consuming tasks that are not time-dependent, like doing the laundry, can be carried out off-peak, provided it’s safe to do so. We offer a range of options including:</p><ul class="mb-3"><li><span class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>Smart Day/Night/Peak</b></span></li><li><span class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>Smart EV Max</b></span></li><li><span class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>Smart Weekends</b></span></li></ul><div class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 !font-bold !text-5xl [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Level 4. Automate your EV & home battery charging, drive energy savings further </div><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">If you have an EV or home battery you may see savings while out and about with our Smart EV Max plan, made for charging your electric vehicle and home energy storage battery – it’s <a rel="" href="/ie/home/news/irelands-longest-overnight-ev-charging-tariff" target="_self" class="Hyperlink">Ireland’s longest overnight EV tariff for home charging</a> from 11pm to 5am. Simply set charging to happen automatically during the cheapest hours via your home battery/EV/EV charger app! </p><div class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 !font-bold !text-5xl [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Level 5. Become a microgenerator, earn credits for low generating months when you export to the grid</div><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"> If you generate electricity from solar panels, you can <a rel="" href="/ie/home/help-centre/microgeneration" target="_self" class="Hyperlink">sell excess power to the grid</a> and receive credits on your bill. In brighter months you can be in credit on your bills which will help keep your bills low in the darker months of the year when exports will not be as high. With a smart plan, you can:</p><ul class="mb-3"><li><span class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>Send excess energy back to the grid</b></span></li><li><span class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>Receive Microgeneration payments as credits on your bill</b></span></li><li><span class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>Maximise the value of your renewable investment</b></span></li></ul><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Your meter makes sure you’re paid fairly for every unit you contribute.</p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>What if you have poor mobile reception?</b></p><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">If network coverage is limited where you live, you can choose Non-Interval (Bi-Monthly) Smart Services, meaning:</p><ul class="mb-3"><li><span class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>Your remote read will be received at least once every two months</b></span></li><li><span class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">You can also <b>submit manual reads</b> to keep your account fully accurate</span></li></ul><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">You still get the benefits, just at a rhythm that suits your connectivity.</p><div class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 !font-bold !text-5xl [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><i>Ready to make your next smart move?</i></div><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><i>Explore all our smart plans in our </i><a rel="" href="/ie/home/smart-hub" target="_self" class="Hyperlink">Smart Hub</a><i>, and take the next step on your smart energy journey.</i></p></div></div><div><div Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.
Read our Privacy Notice.
Read our Cookie Notice.
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
View all individual cookies we use in this category‎

Performance Cookies
Inactive
These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.
Read our Privacy Notice.
Read our Cookie Notice.
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
View all individual cookies we use in this category‎
Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
Inactive
These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

Great Discounts
Switch and get up to 20% discount off our electricity standard unit rates*.
Smarter Energy
Our Smart EV Max tariff* gives you low cost electricity rates between 11pm and 5am. Perfect for powering your home and charging your electric vehicle or home battery with cleaner, greener energy†.

Great discounts from leading retail stores, Dublin Zoo, competitions and more.

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.
Read our Privacy Notice.
Read our Cookie Notice.
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
View all individual cookies we use in this category‎
Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
Inactive
These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.
View all individual cookies we use in this category‎
Functional Cookies
Functional Cookies
Inactive
These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

Targeting Cookies

They are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.
Read our Privacy Notice.
Read our Cookie Notice.
Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
View all individual cookies we use in this category‎
Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
Inactive
These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

Functional Cookies
Functional Cookies
Inactive
These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

Targeting Cookies
Inactive
These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.

Smart meters explained with our smart electricity myth buster
2 July 2024
Share
Categories:
All News
Confused about how to get the most from your smart meter or wondering if signing up for a smart electricity plan is a good idea? Check out our myth buster below to separate smart fact from fiction.
Myth # 1: My smart meter is automatically 'smart'
Fact: You need to ‘activate’ its smart powers by signing up to a smart plan
When your smart meter is installed, your meter readings start being transmitted remotely instead of having to be read manually. ESB Networks collects a reading every two months and sends it to your supplier. This greatly improves your bill accuracy - although the final few days of your bill may still be estimated if your meter-read and billing cycles don't match up perfectly.
Nothing else about your bills will change - if you remain on a standard electricity plan. To receive detailed insights about your energy use and unlock the full benefits of your smart meter, you need to sign up for a smart electricity plan.
Myth # 2: A smart plan will mean higher bills
Fact: If you choose a smart plan that suits your lifestyle, you can reduce your bills
Some smart plans offer different pricing based on when you use electricity. These 'time-of-use' plans are designed to reward off-peak usage by charging less during off-peak hours and slightly more during peak times.  Peak usage in Ireland is early evening, whereas demand is lowest late at night and in the very early hours of the morning.
If you switch to a plan incentivising off-peak use but continue using most of your electricity during peak evening hours (5-7 pm), then it's true, you may well end up paying more.
On the other hand, if you have the flexibility to shift more of your electricity use to off-peak hours, differentiated time-of-use price plans such as our
Smart Day / Night / Peak
offer can save you money.
Other options include our
Smart EV Max plan
, which offers reduced rates at night and very low rates from 11pm am to 5am, so it's ideal for overnight EV charging - or if you have an electricity storage battery you can charge up at night.
Meanwhile, our
Smart Weekend
plan can suit holiday-home owners and households with busy weekends.
The key to making the greatest savings is to understand your usage patterns and choose a plan that matches your lifestyle.
Myth #3: I’m not sure which plan to choose, so it’s best to do nothing
Fact: Our Smart Everyday Plan eliminates the risk of paying more, while providing smart benefits
Our
Smart Everyday
plan is ideal if you're worried about choosing the wrong plan and paying more. You stay on the same flat pricing rate as your current non-smart, standard 24-hour plan, but you get added smart meter benefits. As well as a complete end to estimated bills, you get online access to detailed half-hourly breakdowns of your daily electricity use.
This visibility can help you save energy and money, similar to how a spending journal or food diary improves habits.  It should also help you decide if switching to a time-of-use smart plan like
Smart Weekends
could save you even more.
Myth #4: If I choose a smart plan, I am permanently stuck with that plan
Fact: You can ask your supplier to change you to a different smart plan
It's true that once your smart meter is activated, you can't switch back to a non-smart plan. However, you
can
switch to a different smart plan. If you're an SSE Airtricity customer, you can choose our
Smart Everyday
plan. This plan charges the same flat rate as our standard non-smart plans, but it includes benefits like an end to estimated bills and insights into your electricity usage, so you cannot lose. It's a no-brainer.
Myth #5: Smart plans don’t do anything to help the environment
Fact: Smart metering can help renewable resources, like wind, work harder for us
Electricity is hard to store and must be used as soon as it's generated, making the timing of its use important. During peak times, fossil-fuelled power stations are often needed, while at night, wind turbines are often underutilised.
Smart meters and time-of-use, smart electricity plans incentivise those who have the flexibility to balance their electricity use more evenly throughout the day, evening and night, allowing renewable energy sources like wind to be used more efficiently, reducing fossil fuel dependence and carbon emissions.
Smart meters also offer insights to help households reduce their energy waste, and they help our network operators manage the grid more efficiently. So they are not just good for your pocket; they also help the planet.
Check out
our range of smart meter plans
to find the one that's a perfect fit for you.

How do I sign up for smart meter installation?
ESB Networks
are managing the installation of all smart meters regardless of your energy supplier.
Check below for your current meter type to know how to request a Smart Meter:
Meter type:
How to request:
24 hour / Day and Night / 24 hour meter night storage heating meter.
1.  You can request for a prioritised Smart meter installation through your registered supplier. When contacting your supplier, you'll need your 11-digit MPRN number to hand.
2. If you’ve one of these meter types, you don’t need to do anything as your meter is automatically in the Smart meter exchange programme.
Other meter types
Exchanges are not available for your meter type yet, but we’ll update this section once they’re available.
SAFETY WARNING: As the disconnection and reconnection of electricity may now be performed remotely, it’s essential that you ensure your home, office or site is always treated as live.

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. How to read your smart meter
28 April 2026
Share
Categories:
All News
How to read a smart meter
Smart meters give you clearer insight into your energy use and help make your electricity bills more accurate. Many smart meters send readings automatically, meaning you may not need to submit manual readings at all.
If you have a smart electricity meter and have activated it by switching to a smart plan, the good news is that you won’t need to submit an electricity meter reading.
For those who aren’t on a smart plan, we’ve created this guide on how to read a smart meter.
Do you need to read your smart meter?
Smart meters automatically send electricity meter readings to us via ESB Networks once your meter connection is active. Your experience depends on which type of service you're on:
Non-activated meters
If you have a smart meter but
haven’t switched to a smart plan
yet ESB Networks will read your electricity meter remotely every two months. These readings may not always line up exactly with your billing cycle,
so your electricity bill might be based on a mix of actual and estimated usage
. If you’d like your bill to reflect your usage more precisely for a specific period, you can submit a manual meter reading, or switch to a smart plan.
Interval (30-minute) meters
If you have a smart meter and have
switched to a smart plan,
ESB Networks reads your meter every 30 minutes and sends this data to us once per day. You can view yesterday’s usage in your online account, and
you won’t need to submit electricity meter readings at all!
Your bills will be based on actual electricity usage for the duration of your billing period.
How to read your smart meter manually
First, check if you have a smart meter
You likely have a smart meter if:
Your meter has
a digital screen
(instead of a spinning dial)
The meter model on the front includes the word “
Smart
”
If you’re still unsure, check your online account or contact our Customer Support Team to confirm it for you.
To read your smart meter:
You’ll see your total electricity use in kilowatt hours (kWh) on the main digital display. Just read the numbers on screen from left to right, before the “kWh”, and note them all down.
How to view other smart meter screens
Most smart meters have a single button to cycle through useful information. These additional screens can be helpful if you’re on a day/night rate, peak plan, or generating your own power.
Press once: Date and time
Press twice:
Total usage
Press 3 times
: Night reading (T1)
Press 4 times
: Day reading (T2)
Press 5 times
: Peak-time reading (if applicable to your tariff) (T3)
Press 6 times
: Test screen
Press 7 times
: Export reading (if you generate electricity, shown with a minus symbol)
Where you can submit meter readings (if needed)
There are two ways to submit your meter readings:
Online though ‘
My Account
’ at sseairtricity.com
The
SSE Airtricity App
What smart meters don’t do
Smart meters don’t break down your usage by appliance, and the screen doesn’t give detailed energy insights. It works similarly to a standard digital meter. If you want breakdowns, trends, time-bands, or personalised advice, our
Smart Insights
tool gives all of that and more.
Want deeper insights? Unlock more with Smart Insights
If you’re on a smart plan, you can get clear, detailed visibility of your electricity energy usage and costs so you can make smarter day-to-day decisions with
Smart Insights.
Track your usage and costs by day, month, and year.
See insights by time band and easily spot monthly trends.
Compare today’s usage with the same day last week, including your busiest hour, day, or month.
Check your total usage and spend for the month so far.
Receive personalised tips from your Energy Advisor to help you optimise.
It’s the easiest way to understand your home’s energy story.
Explore all our smart plans in our
Smart Hub
, and take the next step on your smart energy journey.

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.

Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

Performance Cookies
Inactive
These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

accurate. Many smart meters send readings automatically, meaning you may not need to submit manual readings at all. <b>If you have a smart electricity meter and have activated it by switching to a smart plan, the good news is that you won’t need to submit an electricity meter reading. </b>For those who aren’t on a smart plan, we’ve created this guide on how to read a smart meter. </p><div class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 !font-bold !text-5xl [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Do you need to read your smart meter? </div><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Smart meters automatically send electricity meter readings to us via ESB Networks once your meter connection is active. Your experience depends on which type of service you're on:</p><div class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 !font-bold !text-5xl [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>Non-activated meters</b></div><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">If you have a smart meter but <b>haven’t switched to a smart plan</b> yet ESB Networks will read your electricity meter remotely every two months. These readings may not always line up exactly with your billing cycle, <b>so your electricity bill might be based on a mix of actual and estimated usage</b>. If you’d like your bill to reflect your usage more precisely for a specific period, you can submit a manual meter reading, or switch to a smart plan.</p><div class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 !font-bold !text-5xl [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>Interval (30-minute) meters</b></div><p class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">If you have a smart meter and have <b>switched to a smart plan,</b> ESB Networks reads your meter every 30 minutes and sends this data to us once per day. You can view yesterday’s usage in your online account, and <b>you won’t need to submit electricity meter readings at all!</b> Your bills will be based on actual electricity usage for the duration of Just read the numbers on screen from left to right, before the “kWh”, and note them all down.</p><div class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 !font-bold !text-5xl [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]"><b>How to view other smart meter screens</b></div><ul class="mb-3"><li><span class="mb-4 text-neutral-900 leading-[24px] article-body-link text-base [&>iframe]:!h-[446px]">Most smart meters have a single button to cycle through useful information. Top tips for cheaper and more efficient EV charging
Home ev charger with girl in background
9 December 2024
Share
Categories:
All News,
Home Upgrade
Switching to an electric vehicle (EV) is a great way to reduce your carbon footprint and your running costs. And these tips can help make charging as efficient and cost-effective as possible.
Consider a dedicated home charger
You don’t need a dedicated home EV charger to drive an EV. Some owners charge at work or used shared charging points in apartment blocks. Other options include public EV charging stations.
However, if your outside space allows it, installing a dedicated home charger will make your life so much easier.
The cost of buying and having a home charger installed is typically between €800 and €1,200 – minus an
SEAI charger grant of up to €300
– available from the Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI).
This investment is well worthwhile for time savings alone. Compared with a standard socket, a Level 2 home electric car charger (7 kW or higher) can reduce charging time from 8-12 hours down to 4-6 hours, allowing you to fully charge overnight. Visit our
EV Hub
to find out how SSE Airtricity customers can now purchase an Ohme or Zappi electric vehicle charger, complete a quick online home survey and schedule installation — all in one smooth online journey.
Optimise your charging schedule to save money
Charging at home is almost always the cheapest option, costing as little as €3-€5 for a full charge – a no-brainer when compared with the cost of filling a tank of petrol or diesel.
The best way to save on home EV charging is to make sure you’re on the right smart time-of-use electricity plan and take advantage of off-peak electricity rates.
SSE Airtricity’s Smart EV Max plan
is designed specifically for EV drivers who charge at home at night, offering reduced rates for night-time use and super-low rates from 11pm to 5am.
Follow your car manufacturer’s advice on optimum charging limits
Not too long ago, the standard advice was to keep your EV within a 20-80% charge range. While this remains true for some battery types, it’s more of a guideline than a universal rule for other battery types. In fact, some EVs need an occasional full charge to keep the battery management system optimised, while other manufacturers claim that their battery chemistries are designed to handle regular 100% charging without issue.
That said, there are some general strands of truth to the 80:20 charging rule. Just as it’s wise to avoid running an ICE (internal combustion engine) car’s fuel tank down to fumes, keeping an EV’s charge above 20% can be sensible. Similarly, when using public DC high-speed (50 kW or more) fast chargers, stopping at an 80% charge will typically save time and help reduce charger congestion, since charging from 80% to 100% takes roughly the same time as charging to 80%.
Ultimately, the best advice is to follow your car manufacturer’s recommendations for optimal battery care.
Use battery preconditioning
In colder weather, activate your EV’s preconditioning feature (if available) to warm up the battery while it's still plugged in. This keeps the battery at an ideal temperature, reducing energy use during your drive and ensuring optimal performance from the start.
When you're on the road and need to use a DC fast charger, some EV models allow you to set the charging station as a destination in the navigation system. This triggers automatic battery preconditioning, so the battery reaches the ideal temperature by the time you arrive, helping you achieve the fastest possible charging speeds.
By following these tips, you can save money, extend the life of your EV battery and make your charging routine as efficient as possible. Visit our EV Hub to find out more about starting your EV journey and our special products and partner deals tailored for electric vehicle drivers.

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalised web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
Click on the different category headings to view details about all our cookies and to change your default settings.

Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
